description: Inventory core + demo seed data. Implements the P0 inventory database workflow end to end: typed repositories for the core entities, the Inventory list page with fast search/filtering/sorting/pagination (section 29), manual card entry (section 4/43 item 4), individual card management + the Card Detail page (section 30), inventory statuses (section 9), and a comprehensive realistic demo seed (section 44) covering sets/cards/inventory/price snapshots/listings/orders/sales so the UI is never empty. All demo rows are flagged is_demo=1 and clearly labeled in the UI. This makes the app browsable with real-feeling data and establishes the repository + view patterns the remaining features build on.
steps: Reminder: zero deps, `unset NODE_OPTIONS` before any node/npm/tsc; use node:sqlite via the FEAT-001 connection singleton. Read src/db/schema.ts and src/db/connection.ts and the FEAT-001 view/component + repository patterns before starting.

src/repositories/: create typed repositories with prepared statements: setsRepo, cardsRepo, inventoryRepo, storageLocationsRepo, priceSnapshotsRepo (plus thin stubs listingsRepo/ordersRepo/salesRepo if not present, to be fleshed out later). Every user-scoped query MUST take userId. inventoryRepo needs: create, update, getById(userId,id), delete, and a powerful search(userId, {q, setId, rarity, condition, status, minPrice, maxPrice, sku, storageLocationId, classification, sort, page, pageSize}) returning {rows, total} with SQL WHERE building + LIMIT/OFFSET and JOINs to cards/sets for display fields. Include COUNT for pagination.

src/domain/tcg.ts: a TCG-agnostic strategy layer. Define a GameStrategy interface (formatCardTitle, rarityRank, conditionOptions, skuGameCode) and a pokemonStrategy implementation. Card/Set carry a `game` field ('pokemon'). This isolates game-specific formatting per section 47.

src/views/pages/inventory.ts: the Inventory list page - a responsive table (section 31/33) with columns image, name+set+number, rarity badge, condition, qty, market value, target price, status badge, SKU, storage location; a filter/search bar (text search + dropdowns for set/rarity/condition/status + price range) that submits via query params AND supports progressive JS enhancement calling the JSON API; sortable headers; pagination controls. Fast + virtualization-friendly (server pagination, default pageSize 50). Empty state per section 31.

src/api/inventory.ts: JSON endpoints GET /api/inventory (search, same params as repo, returns {rows,total}), POST /api/inventory (create manual entry), PUT/PATCH /api/inventory/:id (update fields incl. status, condition, target price, storage), DELETE /api/inventory/:id. All scoped to session user. Validate inputs; never lose data on partial/invalid input (section 40) - return field-level errors.

src/views/pages/inventory_new.ts + route GET/POST /inventory/new: manual card entry form. Let the user pick an existing card (searchable select backed by /api/cards?q=) OR enter a new card (name, pokemon name, set, number, rarity, type, language, holo/reverse) which upserts into cards, then create the inventory record with condition, quantity, acquisition cost, status (default Unprocessed/Identified), notes. Make entry fast (sensible defaults, keyboard-friendly).

src/api/cards.ts: GET /api/cards?q= for the searchable card picker (name/number/set match), and POST /api/cards to create a card. Scope card creation appropriately (cards/sets are shared reference data, not user-scoped; inventory is user-scoped).

src/views/pages/card_detail.ts + route GET /inventory/:id: the Card Detail page per section 30 - large image (use a neutral placeholder image served from public/ since no external images), full card info, condition, market value, price history (from price_snapshots, rendered as a simple inline SVG sparkline or a small table), listing status, quantity, storage location, cost basis, profit estimate (market_value - acquisition_cost, wiring to the pricing service comes in FEAT-003 but show basic math here), and sections for marketplace listings and sales history (populated from repos). Include inline actions: edit fields, change status.

src/scripts/seed.ts (compiles to dist/scripts/seed.js, run via `npm run seed`): create a demo user (email demo@pokeops.local, a known password, display 'Demo Seller') and seed REALISTIC Pokemon TCG data all flagged is_demo=1: at least 8-10 real-sounding sets (e.g. Obsidian Flames OBF, Paldea Evolved PAL, 151 MEW, Paradox Rift PAR, Scarlet & Violet Base SVI, Temporal Forces TEF, etc. with plausible abbreviations and total counts), ~120+ distinct cards spanning commons/uncommons/rares/holos/reverse holos/full arts/illustration rares/ultra rares/high-value chase cards (include e.g. 'Charizard ex 125/197 Obsidian Flames Ultra Rare'), price_snapshots for the valuable cards (market/low/high/recent sold/competition), inventory records producing a realistic mix: thousands of bulk commons/uncommons (use inventory_lots aggregate rows AND/OR high-quantity inventory rows), a few hundred holos/reverse, ~100-300 higher value singles across statuses (Unprocessed, Identified, Reviewed, Ready to List, Listed, Sold), several storage locations (BOX-A shelf 2 slot 14 etc.), a handful of sample listings, sample orders in various statuses, and sample sales + expenses so profit/analytics later have data. Seed must be idempotent (safe to re-run: clear demo rows or use INSERT OR IGNORE keyed by is_demo). Print a summary of what was seeded and the demo login.
src/views/components: add a small 'Demo data' badge/banner shown when the current user has is_demo inventory, so demo data is clearly distinguished per section 44.

Wire nav: Inventory route, and make Singles/Bulk nav items point to filtered inventory views (Singles = classification/status singles or non-bulk; Bulk placeholder until FEAT-005) so navigation is coherent.

Tests (node:test): src/repositories/inventory.test.ts - seed a temp in-memory/temp-file DB, insert cards + inventory, assert search filters (by rarity, status, price range, text q) and pagination totals are correct; assert user isolation (user B cannot see user A rows). src/scripts/seed.test.ts (or a smaller unit): run the seed against a temp DB and assert counts (>=8 sets, >=100 cards, inventory across multiple statuses, all flagged is_demo) and idempotency (running twice does not duplicate).
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` and `npm test` pass including new inventory + seed tests.

`npm run seed` populates the SQLite DB with >=8 sets, >=100 cards, inventory across all major statuses, storage locations, listings, orders, sales, expenses, all is_demo=1; re-running seed does not duplicate rows.

After seeding + login as demo user, GET /inventory returns 200 with a populated, filterable, paginated table; filtering by rarity/status/price and text search returns correct subsets; GET /api/inventory reflects the same.
Manual card entry via /inventory/new creates a new inventory record (and card if new) visible in the list.
GET /inventory/:id renders the Card Detail page with card info, market value, cost basis, profit estimate, storage location, and price history.
inventory repository search is correctly user-scoped (a test proves user isolation).
verification: unset NODE_OPTIONS; cd /projects/sandbox/PSA && npm run build && npm test
unset NODE_OPTIONS; cd /projects/sandbox/PSA && rm -f data/pokeops.db && npm run seed && npm run seed  (confirm no duplication in the printed summary)

unset NODE_OPTIONS; cd /projects/sandbox/PSA && (npm start & sleep 2; curl -s localhost:4000/api/inventory -H 'Cookie: <session>' | head -c 400; kill %1)  (or exercise via a small node:test integration hitting the router)
findings: Implemented per spec. Router extended with PUT/PATCH/DELETE (main.ts now parses bodies for PUT/PATCH too). Added connection.__setTestDb() hook so repository/seed/router tests can inject an in-memory DatabaseSync (ESM live bindings prevent monkey-patching getDb directly). New repos: sets/cards/storageLocations/priceSnapshots/inventory(full)/listings/orders/sales(thin). TCG strategy at src/domain/tcg.ts also exports INVENTORY_STATUSES + statusTone helpers. Inventory search sort tokens accept +/- prefixes (ascending default for text columns). API bodies read from ParsedBody.json (JSON) or .fields (urlencoded); invalid input returns 422 with field-level errors and never writes bad data. Seed is deterministic (mulberry32 PRNG) and idempotent: clears the demo user's user-owned demo rows + valuable-card price_snapshots, then re-inserts sets/cards via INSERT OR IGNORE keyed by stable ids. Verified: build clean, all 30 tests pass (5 inventory repo + 2 seed + 7 router/API integration), `rm data/pokeops.db && npm run seed && npm run seed` prints identical summaries (10 sets, 135 cards, 184 inventory rows across all 6 statuses, 133 price snapshots, 8 listings, 12 orders, 12 sales, 4 expenses, 3 inventory_lots, 1 demo user - no duplication). Live server smoke test: login as demo user, GET /inventory 200 with 50-row paginated table + Demo banner; /inventory/new, /inventory/:id, /singles, /bulk all 200; /api/inventory filters (rarity/status/condition/price/text) return correct subsets; POST create, PATCH status, DELETE, and 422-on-invalid all confirmed. NOTE for later features: inline `node` one-liners in the shell re-inherit the broken NODE_OPTIONS even after `unset` in the same line if run in certain subshells; prefer `export NODE_OPTIONS=` and background the server within a single command. Singles/Bulk views filter by classification ('single'/'bulk'); Bulk remains a placeholder view until FEAT-005/006.
